headline: India’s Airbound bags $37M to take on trucks with rocket-like drones
summary: Indian startup Airbound has raised $37 million, aiming to make air cargo as cheap as road trucking. They design drones to weigh less than their payload and have completed over 13,000 autonomous flights.
details: Indian startup Airbound has secured $37 million in Series A funding, bringing its total capital raised to nearly $50 million in less than a year. The company aims to make drone-based goods transport as cost-effective as road trucking.

Airbound is redesigning aircraft to be more competitive with ground transportation. Their core innovation involves building vertical-flight drones designed to weigh less than the cargo they carry, addressing the high energy cost of conventional flight.

The current TRT drone weighs about 3.3 pounds and can carry 2.2 pounds of payload. A next version is under development, expected to weigh 6.6 pounds and carry up to 11 pounds, significantly increasing its utility.

The drones use a rocket-like, tail-sitter design, enabling vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) in an upright position before transitioning to horizontal flight. This design avoids dependence on runways, crucial for widespread deployment.

Founded in 2023, Airbound has completed over 13,000 autonomous flights across Bengaluru and Guntur in southern India. This includes more than 1,000 flights transporting diagnostic samples for Narayana Health.

For Narayana Health, a single drone flies samples 2.5 miles in seven minutes, a journey that can take 3-5 hours by truck due to bundling requirements. This partnership is expanding to new facilities designed to rely on drone logistics.

Airbound plans to establish a drone delivery network connecting three cities in Andhra Pradesh, targeting 10,000 flights daily. This ambitious goal would require 250 to 1,000 aircraft, depending on route lengths.

The agreement with the Andhra Pradesh government focuses on regulatory framework development, not contracts or subsidies. Airbound expects to generate revenue from companies utilizing its delivery services.

The startup designs and manufactures its aircraft in a 43,000-square-foot facility in Bengaluru, keeping core systems in-house. Manufacturing capacity is not seen as a bottleneck for scaling operations.

The primary challenge for Airbound's expansion is regulatory approval, particularly for Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) operations. This certification is essential for operating extensive, autonomous delivery networks.

headline: Apple releases public betas for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and more
summary: Following developer beta 7, users can now test upcoming features for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch ahead of their official release.
details: Apple has officially rolled out the public betas for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and other major software updates. This release follows the recent availability of the seventh developer betas for these operating systems, allowing a wider audience to test new features.

Users can now access and provide feedback on the latest iterations of Apple's operating systems. These public betas offer a preview of upcoming enhancements, including potential Siri AI upgrades mentioned in earlier reports, across various Apple devices.
